# Toolbar

A row of controls for one surface, such as an editor's formatting: Button commands and Toggle states, in groups with separators. It is one tab stop, and the arrow keys, Home and End move between its controls (the WAI-ARIA toolbar pattern). Icon-only controls show their label, and any shortcut as `Kbd`, in a tooltip. When the row is too narrow, the controls that do not fit move into a More menu at its end, toggles as checkbox items.

```tsx
import { Toolbar } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/toolbar/toolbar";
```

## Example

```tsx
<Toolbar
  label="Formatting"
  keepFocus
  items={[
    { type: "toggle", label: "Bold", icon: BoldIcon, hideLabel: true, shortcut: ["mod", "b"], pressed: bold, onPressedChange: setBold },
    { type: "toggle", label: "Italic", icon: ItalicIcon, hideLabel: true, shortcut: ["mod", "i"], pressed: italic, onPressedChange: setItalic },
    { type: "separator" },
    { label: "Insert link", icon: LinkIcon, hideLabel: true, shortcut: ["mod", "k"], onClick: insertLink },
  ]}
/>
```

## Usage

`keepFocus` leaves focus in a text editor when a control is pressed with a mouse or a finger, so its selection stays.

## Use instead when

- Use `ToggleGroup` instead for toggles that share one value (text alignment), `ButtonGroup` for a few joined buttons that are one control, and `Menu` with `MenuBar` for an application's menus.

## Props

Type: `ToolbarProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, width, flex and grid placement (`flex-1`, `mt-2`). Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables every control. They stay reachable with the arrow keys. |
| `items` (required) | `readonly ToolbarEntry[]` |  | The controls, in order: buttons, toggles, groups of them and separators. |
| `keepFocus` | `boolean` |  | A press with a mouse or a finger leaves focus where it was, so a text editor beside the toolbar keeps its caret and selection. With nothing focused, the control takes focus as usual. The keyboard still reaches the toolbar with Tab. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | Names the toolbar for screen readers ("Formatting"). It is not shown. |
| `moreLabel` | `string` | `"More"` | The name of the button that opens the controls that do not fit, and its tooltip. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  | The toolbar element (`role="toolbar"`). |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Every control's size, as Button's and Toggle's. |

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `actions`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `items`: `<Toolbar items={[...]}>`.
- `children`: Not a prop. The controls come from `items`: `<Toolbar items={[{ label: "Bold", type: "toggle" }]}>`.
- `orientation`: Not a prop. A Toolbar is a row; controls that do not fit move into its More menu.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`).

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `ToolbarButtonEntry`

A toolbar entry: a command, such as Insert link. The default `type`.

```ts
interface ToolbarButtonEntry extends ToolbarControlEntry {
  type?: "button" | undefined;
  /** Runs when the control is pressed, or chosen from the overflow menu. */
  onClick?: (() => void) | undefined;
}
```

### `ToolbarEntry`

One entry in a Toolbar's `items`: a button (the default `type`), a toggle, a group or a separator.

```ts
type ToolbarEntry = ToolbarButtonEntry | ToolbarToggleEntry | ToolbarGroupEntry | { type: "separator" };
```

### `ToolbarGroupEntry`

A toolbar entry: related controls under a name screen readers hear ("Lists").

```ts
interface ToolbarGroupEntry {
  type: "group";
  /** Names the group for screen readers, and labels it in the overflow menu. */
  label: string;
  items: readonly (ToolbarButtonEntry | ToolbarToggleEntry)[];
}
```

### `ToolbarToggleEntry`

A toolbar entry: an on/off state, such as Bold, drawn as a `Toggle` (`aria-pressed`).

```ts
interface ToolbarToggleEntry extends ToolbarControlEntry {
  type: "toggle";
  /** Whether it is on, when you control it. Pair it with `onPressedChange`. */
  pressed?: boolean | undefined;
  /** Whether it starts on, when the toolbar keeps its state. @default false */
  defaultPressed?: boolean | undefined;
  /** Called with the new state when it is pressed, or chosen from the overflow menu. */
  onPressedChange?: ((pressed: boolean) => void) | undefined;
}
```
